Use Python 3.12 or newer. Extraction writes one `RomFS.img` directly; the build reads it and bundles it as `romfs.img` in the IPA. The app reads the image in place, so neither the Mac build nor the iPhone expands it into a RomFS folder.

**2. Put one game's NSPs in a folder**: the base game (an NSP, or an XCI cartridge dump), plus its update and DLC if you have them:

```
~/Games/MarioWonder/
  Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514000][v0].nsp
  Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514800][v327680].nsp
```

NSZ and XCZ files (compressed NSPs and XCIs) work too: the script converts them once with [nsz](https://github.com/nicoboss/nsz) (`python3 -m pip install nsz`) and keeps the NSPs in `<title ID>_build/nsp/`, which takes their full size on disk.

projects.readme_intro: Play your own Nintendo Switch games natively on iPhone and iPad. Bring your game (its NSP files) and your `prod.keys`; one script turns them into an IPA that you sideload. It is not an emulator: the game's own code runs directly on the Apple chip, with Switch graphics rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from any game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo or any game publisher. > [!TIP] > **Prefer an app to the command line?** [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple) is a community Mac app that builds your games for the iPhone, iPad or Mac, keeps the Mac games in a library and starts them with their settings. projects.description: Native MLX runtime for Laya typed decision models — 7–14 ms short decisions on M3 Max. No text generation, PyTorch, or cloud API.
projects.readme_excerpt:
```bash
pip install laya-mlx
```

```python
import laya_mlx as laya

agent = laya.load("aac6fef/laya-mlx")
result = agent.predict(
    "I was billed twice. Please refund the duplicate.",
    {
        "department": {
            "type": "choice",
            "instructions": "Who should handle this?",
            "criteria": ["billing", "technical", "sales"],
        }
    },
)
print(result["answers"]["department"])
```

Apple Silicon, Python 3.11+, macOS 14+. First load downloads the checkpoint; later inference is fully local. The measured environment is macOS 27.2, Python 3.12.13 and MLX 0.32.2. That MLX release supplies macOS 14, 15 and 26 wheels; the local installer selected the 26 wheel. Older supported macOS versions were not tested on this machine.

Run the terminal demo:

```bash
pip install 'laya-mlx[demo]'
hf download aac6fef/laya-multilingual-mlx
laya-snake
```

Download once before the offline demo. Use a terminal at least 104 × 35 cells. Space pauses, ↑/↓ changes speed, R resets and Q quits. `laya-snake --max-speed` makes a fresh decision for every move without pacing.
